name: CUDA GPU computing platform
description: A programming platform and software environment for running general-purpose parallel computation on supported NVIDIA graphics processors.

date.label: November 2006
date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: NVIDIA introduced CUDA as a GPU parallel-computing platform.

evidence.supports: NVIDIA guide dates introduction and describes the programming platform.

events.caveats: Introduction is distinct from toolkit release and does not demonstrate application adoption.

evidence.supports: NVIDIA guide dates introduction and describes the programming platform.

date.label: 26 June 2007
date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: NVIDIA announced availability of CUDA Toolkit and SDK version 1.0.
events.caveats: Compatible GPUs, drivers and supported operating systems were required; this release was not support for all graphics hardware.

evidence.supports: NVIDIA announces the 1.0 toolkit and SDK.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced event establishing this scoped achievement; it is not a claim of global priority.

caveats: General-purpose computation on graphics hardware and parallel programming predated CUDA; later toolkit features and adoption require separate evidence.

research.note: New source-backed draft; independent review pending. Independent reader checked NVIDIA’s retrospective 2006 introduction and its 2007 toolkit/SDK availability announcement.
